h1: Budgeting a beer brand launch in India in rupees, line by line
title: Budgeting a Beer Brand Launch in India | Craft Beer School
desc: A line by line framework for budgeting a beer brand launch in India: brand work, label approval, packaging, launch stock, sales, events and contingency.
teaser: Most beer launch budgets in India miss the same lines: label registration, slow-moving stock and the second print run.
standfirst: A beer brand launch in India costs far more than the design and the first batch. Here is a line by line framework to build your budget in rupees from real quotes, so the money lasts until the beer starts selling.
sections: Why a line by line budget matters

Founders often budget a beer launch as two numbers: the brewing cost and a marketing figure. The money then runs out somewhere between label approval and the third month of sales, when stock is sitting in a warehouse and the distributor wants support. A line by line budget shows where every rupee goes and, more usefully, which lines you forgot.

We cannot give you prices. They vary by city, volume, supplier and year. Any number we printed would be wrong for someone. What we can give you is the structure we use, so you can fill it with your own quotes.

1. Strategy and naming. Positioning, audience, name shortlist and language checks. Some founders do this themselves. Others pay a consultant or agency.
  2. Trademark. Searches and filing in the relevant classes, usually through an attorney. Budget for possible objections, which add time and fees. Our guide to brewery name trademarks explains the process.
  3. Identity and pack design. Logo, colours, type, label or can artwork for each beer and the brand book. Ask designers to quote for the full range rather than one label. Ask for print-ready files for each format too.

1. Label approval and registration. Most states require label and brand registration with excise, often renewed yearly. Some charge per label or per brand. Fees vary by state and change, so ask a licensing consultant for the current schedule in each state you plan to sell in. Add their fee too.
  2. Packaging materials. Cans or bottles, labels or sleeves, crowns or ends, cartons and trays. Get quotes at your real launch volume. Minimum order quantities often force you to buy more than the first batch needs, so budget for the cash tied up in stock. Our guide to beer packaging costs breaks down the per-unit maths.
  3. Proofs and reprints. At least one round of printed proofs, plus a reserve for a reprint if approval forces a change. Most first launches need one.
Line 7 to 9: getting beer to market

1. Launch stock. The cost of brewing and packaging your first runs, whether in your own brewery or under contract. Include the duty and taxes due at the brewery gate, which in many states are paid before the beer earns anything.
  2. Distribution and trade margins. The share taken by distributors and retailers, plus any listing or placement costs. These vary widely by state and channel. Our guide to beer distribution in India covers how the chain works.
  3. Sales team. Salaries, travel and phone costs for the people who visit outlets. Budget at least six months before a new brand can pay for its own sales effort.

1. Point of sale and samples. Shelf strips, staff cards, tasting stock and glassware for trade launches. Product used for tasting has a real cost, including duty.
  2. Events and launch night. Venue, food, staff and permits for a trade or consumer launch. Many states need specific event licences for serving alcohol, so check before you book.
  3. Digital and content. Photography, video, website and social media work. Paid promotion of alcohol is heavily restricted in India, so most of this budget goes on content and community, not ads.

Add a contingency of at least 10 to 15 percent of everything above. Launches run late, approvals stall, a print run comes out wrong or a big order needs a second batch faster than planned. Founders who skip this line usually find it the hard way.

A real cost that catches many launches: the beer that does not sell in time. Hoppy beers lose freshness fast in Indian heat. Stock sitting in warm warehouses may need to be withdrawn. Budget for some write-off on your first runs, especially for beers with a short shelf life.

Build the budget in a spreadsheet with a row per line, three supplier quotes where possible and a month-by-month cash column. The cash view matters most: duty, packaging and design bills land months before sales income arrives. Compare it with your available funding and decide what to cut before you start, rather than halfway through.

Then check it against your brand plan. If the plan relies on a launch event and you have budgeted nothing for it, one of them has to change. A budget that matches the brand strategy is one you can actually follow.
faqs: How much does it cost to launch a beer brand in India?
It depends on volume, the number of states, packaging format and how much work you outsource. Build a line by line budget from real quotes rather than relying on a single figure.
Do I need to pay for label registration in every state?
Most states require their own label and brand registration. Fees vary. Ask a licensing consultant for the current process in each state you plan to sell in.
How much contingency should a beer launch budget have?
At least 10 to 15 percent of the total. Delays, reprints and unsold stock are common in first launches.
